The FOMC held the target range at 5.25–5.50% and kept QT caps unchanged ($60B UST, $35B MBS), with operational settings consistent with the floor system (IORB 5.4%, ON RRP 5.3%, ON repo min 5.5%). Guidance remains data dependent and attentive to “cumulative tightening” and policy lags, keeping policy restrictive until inflation returns to 2% amid low unemployment and gradually easing inflation.

FSR context tilts risks modestly more negative for growth despite a resilient core system. The report underscores: a sound and resilient banking system with stabilization aided by facilities like the BTFP; but notable vulnerabilities from higher long-term rates that can strain market liquidity, structural fragilities in money market funds and other nonbank intermediation, concentrated hedge fund exposures in Treasury markets, and refinancing pressures in commercial real estate. It also flags macro risks (public debt, geopolitical tensions, China weakness) and tighter bank lending standards, all of which can amplify the drag from restrictive policy.

Netting these, the communication is still supportive of disinflation credibility but, through an FSR lens, slightly more negative for the near-term growth outlook than a purely macro read.
